title: Non-blocking follow-up from backend-profit-target-weekly-channel-followups-followups-followups PR #307 review
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #307 (backend-profit-target-weekly-channel-followups-followups-followups, aligning check_profit_target_wording.py's run-based dedup key to (pattern_index, lineno) and adding 3 regression tests). PR #307's blocking finding (the nested-f-string regression test not genuinely exercising _find_fstring_end_index's depth-tracking branch) sent the task itself back to implementing -- this is a separate, independently-verified, non-blocking gap found during the same review pass, worth tracking so it isn't lost once the parent task re-merges.

checklist.step: `_find_run_violations`'s `reported` dedup set is local to a single implicit-concatenation-run invocation, both before and after PR #307's dedup-key change from `lineno`-only to `(pattern_index, lineno)`. Two *separate* implicit-concatenation runs that happen to sit on the same physical source line (e.g. two statements separated by a semicolon, each its own run) and both match the same banned pattern each get their own fresh `reported` set inside `_find_run_violations`, so `check_banned_patterns` ends up emitting two duplicate violation strings for the same `(pattern_index, lineno)` instead of deduping across runs. Verified directly: `x = "today's " "Autoenvelope"; y = "today's " "Autoenvelope"` on one line produces 2 identical violation strings both on `main` before PR #307 and after it -- confirming PR #307's dedup-key change did not introduce this (per the parent task's own verification ask), but also that it didn't fix this pre-existing, narrower gap either. Cosmetic duplicate reporting only (the guard still correctly fails and points at the right line; no missed regression), and the two-runs-on-one-line shape it requires (semicolon-separated statements using implicit string concatenation) isn't used anywhere in this codebase's actual style today. Worth threading a per-file `reported` set into `_find_run_violations` (or having `check_banned_patterns` dedupe across all of a file's per-run violations at the call site) so a rare same-line multi-run case doesn't double-count, for the same dedup-granularity-consistency reason PR #307's own fix cited. RESOLVED: `_find_run_violations` now takes `reported` as a parameter, and `check_banned_patterns` creates one `run_reported` set per file (not per run) and passes it into every `_find_run_violations` call for that file's runs. Added `test_two_semicolon_separated_runs_matching_same_pattern_on_one_line_dedupe`, reproducing the exact repro from this checklist item (two semicolon-separated implicit-concat statements matching the same pattern on one line) -- confirmed it produces 2 identical violations against the pre-fix code (verified directly against the `HEAD` copy of the script in an isolated scratch run) and exactly 1 after the fix.

(Round 2 review, PR #307) The parent task's checklist item 8 was marked `done: true` with a 'RESOLVED' note, but that note only closes half of what item 8's own text named as needing a regression test: `_find_fstring_end_index`'s nesting-depth-tracking branch (now genuinely covered by the new `test_find_fstring_end_index_tracks_nesting_depth`, independently reproduced by both pr-reviewer and a backgrounded `code-review` (effort high) pass) and its defensive fallback `return start_index` (still completely untested). Confirmed independently via `coverage run --branch --include="*/check_profit_target_wording.py" -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: line 319 (the fallback) remains in the Missing set after PR #307, unchanged from before it. This is not a live bug -- the fallback only triggers if `tokenize.generate_tokens` produced an unbalanced FSTRING_START/FSTRING_END stream, which per the function's own comment 'shouldn't happen' for a stream tokenize itself produced without raising -- but it is trivially testable directly (call `_find_fstring_end_index` with a hand-built, deliberately-unbalanced token list, the same direct-unit-test technique PR #307 already used for the depth-tracking branch), so this isn't a case of genuinely unreachable code that can't be exercised. Not filed as blocking on PR #307 itself since the fix genuinely resolves the round-1 blocking finding (the tautological test) and the fallback gap is inert defensive code, not a correctness risk -- but worth closing given this exact function's history of three separate axes of bugs across 6+ review rounds, and worth being explicit that checklist item 8's 'RESOLVED'/done:true claim overstates what was actually locked in with a test. RESOLVED: added `test_find_fstring_end_index_returns_start_index_when_unbalanced`, calling `_find_fstring_end_index` directly with a hand-built two-token list (`FSTRING_START` followed by an unrelated `NAME` token, no matching `FSTRING_END` anywhere), confirming it returns `start_index` unchanged. Re-ran `coverage run --branch --include="*/check_profit_target_wording.py" -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: line 319 no longer appears in the Missing set.

decisions.decision: The new per-file `run_reported` set threaded into `_find_run_violations` (item 1) is kept entirely separate from the ordinary per-line scan's own local `reported` set in `check_banned_patterns` -- not merged into one shared set across both checks.
decisions.rationale: The two checks are already documented as mutually exclusive by design: `_find_run_violations`'s own docstring states a match is only ever reported there when the per-line scan couldn't already see it directly in the untouched original text (i.e. it crosses a piece boundary or a real embedded newline within one piece). A match entirely on one physical line within one piece is explicitly left to the per-line scan and skipped by the run-based one (see `test_phrase_entirely_within_one_run_member_is_not_double_reported`). Since the two checks by construction never emit the same `(pattern_index, lineno)` key for the same underlying match, merging their dedup sets would add coupling and complexity for no behavioral difference; keeping the run-based dedup set genuinely per-file-and-run-scope-only (not also spanning the line-scan) is the narrowest change that fixes the reported bug (duplicate reports across multiple runs) without touching the already-correct, already-tested per-line-scan behavior. Alternative considered and rejected: having `check_banned_patterns` share one `reported` set across both the per-line scan and every run in the file -- rejected as broader than what the checklist item asked for and riskier given this function's 7+ round review history, where every past fix attempt introduced its own new edge case.
